card.name: Ring shout
card.tagline: America’s deepest sacred dance — counterclockwise circle worship, born in plantation ‘praise houses,’ still danced in coastal Georgia today.
card.profile: The ring shout is a distinctive African American ritual dance originating with enslaved Africans in the southern United States where worshippers move in a counterclockwise circle while hand-clapping, foot-patting and shuffling, stick-beating to foreground the rhythm, and call-and-response singing. It is an oral tradition passed down in African American families since the era of slavery. Elders and religious leaders pass down songs and shouts to the younger generation.
card.insight: Musicologist and educator Eileen Southern traced the earliest observance of the ring shout to a 1819 observance of the secret African ritual dances that took place later in the Black quarters of Philadelphia after a Christian camp meeting. Helena Island in South Carolina from 1862 to 1863 and documented several ring shout experiences in praise houses.
